name: Platform Adoption Essentials
description: The Platform Adoption Kernel establishes the universal foundation for platform transformations, organized into the three Areas of Concern.

focuses.name: Value
focuses.description: Focuses on business justification, financial management, and organizational alignment.

focuses.name: Solution
focuses.description: Encapsulates the design, provisioning, optimization, and the hosted items running on the platform foundation.

focuses.name: Endeavor
focuses.description: Governs the execution of the transformation, encompassing people, processes, and policies.

alphas.name: Opportunity
alphas.description: The foundational business drivers dictating the platform transformation.

states.name: Initiated
states.description: The desire to adopt a platform is identified.

states.name: Determined
states.description: The value and parameters of the platform are quantified.

states.name: Value Established
states.description: The platform's value is accepted by sponsors.

states.name: Viable
states.description: The business case demonstrates a viable return.

states.name: Addressed
states.description: The opportunity is actively being addressed by the platform.

states.name: Benefit Accrued
states.description: The expected benefits are being consistently realized.

alphas.name: Platform Value And Economics
alphas.description: The financial and outcome-based justification and accounting for the platform.

states.name: Modeled
states.description: Financial needs and potential values are recognized.

states.name: Allocated
states.description: Costs and benefits are logically modeled.

states.name: Sustained
states.description: The economic model is approved.

alphas.name: Stakeholders
alphas.description: The individuals, groups, or organizations affected by, or able to affect, the platform.

states.name: Recognized
states.description: Key stakeholders are identified.

states.name: Represented
states.description: Stakeholder representatives are designated.

states.name: Involved
states.description: Stakeholders actively participate.

states.name: In Agreement
states.description: Stakeholder expectations are aligned.

states.name: Satisfied for Deployment
states.description: Stakeholders approve deployment.

states.name: Satisfied in Use
states.description: Stakeholders are satisfied with the operational platform.

alphas.name: Requirements
alphas.description: The capabilities, features, and constraints the platform must satisfy.

states.name: Conceived
states.description: The need for a specific asset is identified.

states.name: Bounded
states.description: The scope of the requirements is defined.

states.name: Coherent
states.description: Requirements are clear, consistent, and logical.

states.name: Acceptable
states.description: Stakeholders agree the requirements meet their needs.

states.name: Addressed
states.description: The platform satisfies the established requirements.

states.name: Fulfilled
states.description: All requirements are successfully delivered and operational.

alphas.name: Platform
alphas.description: The unified system of assets and interfaces provided to consumers.

states.name: Architecture Selected
states.description: The foundational structure is chosen.

states.name: Baselined
states.description: Core capabilities are established.

states.name: Provisioned
states.description: The platform can be consumed.

states.name: Ready
states.description: The platform is fully operational.

states.name: Hosting Assets
states.description: The platform is actively supporting workloads.

states.name: Evolving
states.description: The platform is decommissioned.

alphas.name: Platform Consumption Interface
alphas.description: The means by which consumers interact with and consume platform assets.

states.name: Envisioned
states.description: The desired interface is conceptualized.

states.name: Scoped
states.description: Interface capabilities are defined.

states.name: Available
states.description: The interface is accessible.

states.name: Self Service
states.description: Consumers can independently use the interface.

states.name: Optimized
states.description: The interface provides a frictionless experience.

alphas.name: Platform Asset
alphas.description: The individual services, tools, or resources that constitute the platform.

states.name: Identified
states.description: The need for a specific asset is identified.

states.name: Specified
states.description: Asset requirements are detailed.

states.name: Provisioned
states.description: The asset is created or acquired.

states.name: Integrated
states.description: The asset works within the broader platform.

states.name: Operational
states.description: The asset is in active use.

states.name: Value Yielding
states.description: The asset is decommissioned.

alphas.name: Work
alphas.description: The activities required to build, operate, and maintain the platform.

states.name: Initiated
states.description: Work is requested.

states.name: Prepared
states.description: Work is ready to begin.

states.name: Started
states.description: Work is in progress.

states.name: Under Control
states.description: Work is proceeding predictably.

states.name: Concluded
states.description: Work is finished.

states.name: Closed
states.description: All work activities are officially complete.

alphas.name: Team
alphas.description: The group of individuals responsible for the platform's success.

states.name: Seeded
states.description: Initial team members are identified.

states.name: Formed
states.description: The team structure is established.

states.name: Collaborating
states.description: Team members work together effectively.

states.name: Performing
states.description: The team consistently delivers value.

states.name: Adjourned
states.description: The team is disbanded or repurposed.

alphas.name: Way Of Working
alphas.description: The tailored set of practices, tools, operational workflows, and industry alignments used by a team.

states.name: Principles Established
states.description: The principles, constraints, and baseline industry alignments are established.

states.name: Foundation Established
states.description: The key practices, workflow models, and logical definitions are selected.

states.name: In Use
states.description: Team members are using behavioral walkthroughs to adapt to the way-of-working.

states.name: In Place
states.description: The practices are fully integrated into daily activities.

states.name: Working Well
states.description: The way of working is highly efficient, automated, and demonstrably successful.

states.name: Retired
states.description: The way of working is no longer needed.

states.name: Scoped
states.description: The need for governance is recognized.

states.name: Documented
states.description: Initial policies are defined.

states.name: Audited
states.description: Policies are actively applied.

alphas.name: Platform Risk And Compliance
alphas.description: Measures the business risk evaluation, security posture validation, and compliance mitigation maturity.

states.name: Identified
states.description: Basic security risks and compliance needs are listed.

states.name: Assessed
states.description: Detailed risk assessment matrices and compliance mappings are documented.

states.name: Mitigated
states.description: Scenario-based behavioral guides mitigate specific user risks.

states.name: Automated
states.description: Automated compliance auditing and security posture checks are in place.

alphas.name: Organizational Change
alphas.description: The organizational patterns, business rationale, and change management required to support the platform transformation.

states.name: Recognized
states.description: Rationale for change is identified.

states.name: Strategized
states.description: Change plans and communication pathways are mapped.

states.name: Enabled
states.description: Playbooks addressing behavioral pushback are executed.

states.name: Embedded
states.description: Comprehensive change management toolkits and automated feedback surveys are deployed.

competencies.name: Platform Security And Compliance Enforcement
competencies.description: The ability to design, implement, and automate security policies, access controls, and compliance checks within the platform.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands basic security principles and compliance requirements.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can configure basic security settings and access controls based on documented procedures.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Can independently design and implement comprehensive security architectures and automate compliance auditing.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can adapt security strategies to address novel threats and complex, multi-cloud environments.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Develops new paradigms for platform security and proactive threat hunting.

competencies.name: Platform Strategic Alignment
competencies.description: The ability to align platform capabilities and roadmap with broader business goals, economic models, and enterprise architecture.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the high-level business drivers for the platform.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can articulate how specific platform features support identified business opportunities.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Can develop and manage platform roadmaps that demonstrably drive business value and ROI.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can pivot platform strategy in response to shifting market conditions or major organizational changes.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Pioneers new platform business models or economic strategies that redefine enterprise value.

competencies.name: Site Reliability
competencies.description: The ability to apply software engineering principles to operations, ensuring platform reliability, scalability, and performance (SRE).

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the concepts of SLIs, SLOs, and basic incident response.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can participate in incident response and implement basic monitoring alerts.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Can independently design robust monitoring systems, define effective SLOs, and lead complex incident resolutions.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can architect highly resilient, self-healing systems and establish enterprise-wide SRE practices.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Develops novel approaches to chaos engineering or predictive reliability modeling.

competencies.name: Stakeholder Representation

levels.name: Masters

levels.name: Adapts

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Recognized expert, able to extend representation concepts to new contexts.

narrativeTypes.name: The STAR Format
narrativeTypes.description: Enforces a strict cause-and-effect relationship between context and outcomes (Situation, Task, Action, Result).

narrativeElements.name: Situation
narrativeElements.description: The context or background of the challenge.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the specific situation, context, or baseline state before action is taken.

narrativeElements.name: Task
narrativeElements.description: The specific challenge, objective, or requirement.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Outline the specific task, problem, or goal that needs to be addressed.

narrativeElements.name: Action
narrativeElements.description: The specific steps or interventions performed.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Detail the methodology, activities, or steps taken to address the task.

narrativeElements.name: Result
narrativeElements.description: The outcome, impact, or value achieved.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Summarize the measurable results, outcomes, or state changes achieved from the actions.

narrativeTypes.name: The Hero's Journey
narrativeTypes.description: Highly effective for macro-level lifecycle orchestrations (platform adoptions, transformations).

narrativeElements.name: The Ordinary World
narrativeElements.description: The starting point before the transformation.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the current, pre-platform state of the organization.

narrativeElements.name: The Call to Adventure
narrativeElements.description: The catalyst for change.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Outline the business opportunity, crisis, or driver that necessitates the platform transformation.

narrativeElements.name: The Ordeal
narrativeElements.description: The core transformation challenges and execution.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Detail the complex adoption activities, migrations, and challenges faced during implementation.

narrativeElements.name: The Return
narrativeElements.description: The new operational baseline and realized value.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the successful adoption, the accrual of benefits, and the new optimized way of working.

narrativeTypes.name: The Three-Act Structure & StoryBrand
narrativeTypes.description: Positions the consumer as the Hero and the Platform Engineering team as the Guide utilizing the defined approach.

narrativeElements.name: Act I: The Hero and the Problem
narrativeElements.description: Identifying the consumer and their pain points.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Identify the primary consumer (the Hero) and detail the specific friction or problem they face.

narrativeElements.name: Act II: The Guide and the Plan
narrativeElements.description: The platform team offers a solution.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Introduce the Platform Engineering team as the Guide who provides a clear, paved-path approach or plan.

narrativeElements.name: Act III: Call to Action and Success
narrativeElements.description: Execution and outcome.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the call to action for the consumer to adopt the plan, and the successful outcome of doing so.

narrativeTypes.name: Micro-Narratives (ABT)
narrativeTypes.description: Shorter frameworks (And/But/Therefore) designed for rapid, highly persuasive daily execution updates.

narrativeElements.name: And (Context)
narrativeElements.description: The current situation and baseline facts.
narrativeElements.howToUse: State the current agreed-upon context, background, and baseline facts.

narrativeElements.name: But (Conflict)
narrativeElements.description: The problem, challenge, or contradiction.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Introduce the specific problem, blocker, challenge, or contradiction encountered.

narrativeElements.name: Therefore (Resolution)
narrativeElements.description: The action taken or conclusion reached.
narrativeElements.howToUse: State the specific action taken, decision made, or conclusion reached to resolve the conflict.

narrativeTypes.name: User story
narrativeTypes.description: A brief, informal explanation of a software feature written from the perspective of the end user.

narrativeElements.name: As a [role]
narrativeElements.description: This identifies the specific persona or role interacting with the feature. It avoids the generic term **the user** to provide context on their technical ability, permissions, and needs.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to define constraints. Instead of saying "user," say "First-time Visitor" or "System Administrator." This helps the developers understand if the UI should be "idiot-proof" or "power-user focused."

narrativeElements.name: I wan to [perform some action]
narrativeElements.description: This is the intent or the feature itself. It describes the action the user wants to take within the software.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Keep this focused on the **what,** not the **how.** Avoid mentioning specific UI elements like **click a red button.** Focus on the functional capability you are giving them.

narrativeElements.name: So that [I can achieve some goal]
narrativeElements.description: This is the purpose. It explains the underlying problem the user is trying to solve or the value they hope to gain.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to justify the work. If you can’t find a compelling **So that** statement, the feature might not be worth building. It also helps developers suggest better technical solutions if they understand the ultimate goal.

narrativeTypes.name: Epic
narrativeTypes.description: A well-structured Epic provides a "north star" for the team, ensuring everyone knows why a large project exists and what success looks like.

narrativeElements.name: Summary
narrativeElements.description: A clear, punchy title and a one-sentence elevator pitch that describes the high-level initiative.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Treat this as the project's identity. Use it in stakeholder meetings and roadmap views to provide an instant understanding of what is being built without getting bogged down in details.

narrativeElements.name: Strategic Intent
narrativeElements.description: This section explains how this Epic aligns with the company's broader business goals or quarterly objectives (OKRs).
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to justify the budget and resource allocation. If you can't link the Epic back to a specific business value (e.g., "Increasing retention by 10%"), it shouldn't be an Epic.

narrativeElements.name: User Personas
narrativeElements.description: A list of the primary and secondary users who will be impacted by this large-scale change.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to keep the scope focused. When brainstorming features, ask: "Does this specific feature serve the personas listed in the Epic?" If not, it belongs in a different Epic.

narrativeElements.name: High-Level Requirements
narrativeElements.description: These are not detailed stories yet, but rather the broad capabilities the system must have once the Epic is finished.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use these as "themes" to help you brainstorm the individual User Stories later. They serve as the framework for your backlog.

narrativeElements.name: Success Metrics
narrativeElements.description: The quantitative data points that will prove the Epic was a success after it is released.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to define the "Definition of Done" for the entire project. Instead of saying "when the code is finished," use "when the checkout conversion rate hits 5%."

narrativeTypes.name: Lifecycle
narrativeTypes.description: A standard lifecycle orchestration framework to map progression phases.

narrativeElements.name: Prerequisites
narrativeElements.description: Conditions required before starting the lifecycle.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Define the Phase 0 or preparation steps, including baseline checks or prerequisite states, that must be achieved before the main lifecycle begins.

narrativeElements.name: Lifecycle Phase
narrativeElements.description: An active stage of lifecycle execution.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Detail the active state transitions, required work products, and activities for this specific phase of the lifecycle progression.
